intuition.title: Self-trapped-exciton emission
intuition.summary: The authors interpret the broad, strongly Stokes-shifted emission and microsecond-scale decays in the context of self-trapped excitons. Their model describes free carriers becoming self-trapped through strong electron–phonon interactions, followed by slow radiative decay. This is a mechanistic interpretation, not a directly observed intermediate state.
intuition.scope: Author interpretation or model, as qualified in the linked main-only review; not a direct measurement or batch-specific claim.

intuition.title: Possible causes of PL loss in solution
intuition.summary: For solution samples, the authors suggest PL loss may relate to NC aggregation or surface oxidation of Cu+ to Cu2+. They report no noticeable XRD structural change after UV excitation in humid air for 1 h and infer that bulk crystalline phase formation is unlikely to explain the PL loss. These alternatives are not distinguished by the reported comparison.

general_background.title: Carboxylic-acid and carboxylate ligands
general_background.summary: Carboxylic acids and carboxylates can associate with metal-containing surfaces and solution species through their oxygen groups. The hydrocarbon part of a long-chain ligand can favour dispersion in a compatible solvent, while acid-base equilibria influence how its head group associates.

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
